utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. Good morning. Good morning to you all; ladies and gentlemen; good morning to the technical booth and the interpreters, the Registry staff, the Office of the Prosecutor and Defence counsel. I see that everybody is present. We're going to take up the case where we left off, but before we do that, I should like to draw the attention of Mr. Krstan Simic to the fact that we're still having some problems with regard to your request for protective measures. I think that there was a problem of the system of numbering the pseudonyms. That was one point. Secondly, the identification of witnesses for safe conduct, safe passage. So perhaps you could contact the registrar to clarify those points. As far as I know, we have had one request asking for protective measures for a number of witnesses, that is to say, pseudonyms, and also a request asking for safe conduct, safe passage. Now, I was given to understand that at the last Status Conference, with regard to the safe conduct request, you withdrew that request, but then I think that I heard yesterday that you would like to retain that request. So now I am asking you which witnesses are asking for safe conduct, and they all need to -- their identities need to be established. So would you please contact the registrar to clear up the matter so that we can take a decision. But we must have concrete elements and all the facts for us to be able to make a ruling. Well, there we have it. Would you like to add anything, Mr. Krstan Simic, to that? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. There seems to be a misunderstanding that I withdrew the request, but as that is a thing of the past, yesterday we handed in to the Registry all the facts, and we have aligned our numbering system. So I think that the process has been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I myself asked the registrar which persons benefited from the safe conduct, and they told me that we needed a full identification, not only the names of the witnesses but all the other data as well. But let me ask Madam Registrar how things stand with respect to that issue.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We need -- for the witnesses who require safe conduct, we need their address, we need their date of birth, we need their full name and, once we have that, then we can issue a safe conduct certificate. So during the break, I will get with Mr. Simic and Mr. Lukic, and we will finalise everything and make sure we have all the necessary information. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And please make a note of the fact that before a permit for safe conduct is issued, you need a ruling from the Trial Chamber, of course.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think we can now have the witness introduced into the courtroom for the cross-examination. I don't think any other members of the Defence teams had any questions to ask the witness, and I think it is now up to Ms. Somers to have the cross-examination. Are you ready for that, Ms. Somers?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And I want to thank you very much for giving us the evening to get ourselves together in this sort of mix-up. I would like to inform the Chamber ahead of time that a number of the documents which we wish to put in were to have been translated today, but because of the change, we're slightly disadvantaged. Therefore, if the Chamber will permit me, I will, at this stage, ask the registrar to put on the ELMO a document, and I don't know if a copy has been provided to the interpreters, but if I make reference, I may actually have to ask the witness to assist in reading out of it, and we will, of course, provide, within just a matter of days, perhaps by tomorrow, the essential translations. My apologies again. It was a function of the change that just threw us off a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can. Good morning to you too, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You are now going to continue your testimony by answering questions put to you by the Prosecutor, Ms. Susan Somers, in this case. Ms. Susan Somers, your witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, yesterday you indicated that you left Zagreb in September of 1991; is that correct? Is it September of 1991?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did you leave your work in Zagreb? Did you physically leave Zagreb in September or did you simply -- or what did you do in September?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I physically left Zagreb, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I thought maybe you might be able to help us understand a document, though.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I would have to ask the registrar to present it again. As I've indicated to the Chamber, it is in its rather raw form. But if you have the pile of documents, it would be dated the 27th of October, 1992, and it bears the number P0048810. It is a three-page document. If it is too difficult, I'm happy to turn my copy over to the registrar right now. Otherwise, we can present it. Is there one that's possibly available for the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, the document which is on the ELMO, which is on the projector before you, is dated the 27th of October, 1992. It is from the -- essentially from the Serb Republic Ministry of Internal Affairs, the CSB Banja Luka, and the Public Safety Station for Prijedor. Turning your attention to the second page of the document, item 4, it says: "Basrak Lazar," and then, "son of Ranko." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Is this you? Is this about you?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Tell me, please, the date of separation from Zagreb service is listed in the last line. Does it not say the 7th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the date when my wife went to Zagreb to fetch my documents. I left and failed to sever my employment ties.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You just walked out of your job?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you leave there as a police officer in good standing, having walked out of your job? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] The witness has said that he fled from Zagreb because of the threats he had been receiving and because he felt unsafe. Five hundred thousand Serbs left Croatia, let me mention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic, objection rejected. Please continue, Ms. Somers. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So we have your wife returning to Zagreb, a place from which you fled, to get your documents because essentially you were absent without leave or you essentially walked out on your job; correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Now, when you went to Bosnia, when you went back, you immediately found employment as a police officer? Immediately?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What did you do between the time you arrived in Bosnia and the time you became a police officer? Would you give us the date you were actually made a police officer in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Where did you serve as a police officer as of the 1st of July, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Police Station 1 in Prijedor -- Prijedor Police Station 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you physically sitting in Prijedor -- well, what part of Prijedor? Is that in the town of Prijedor, or where is that?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the town of Prijedor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: July 1st, 1992. Maybe you can clarify. Did you tell us yesterday that Kvocka arrived in Tukovi July 1st, 1992?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: How do you know, sitting in Prijedor town police department, or police centre, however you wish to define it - we've been a little loose in our terms - how do you know what he did, what he said, what was said about him, to watch out for him if he was in Tukovi and you were in Prijedor? Can you explain that? Help us understand.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was a reserve policeman before that in the police station in Tukovi and I was up there during that time. I received my decision --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Which time? Please be specific.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The decision about my employment, I received sometime at the end of July, that is to say, that I had been taken into the service from the 1st of July, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You received a decision about your employment at the end of July and yet you were able to start on the 1st of July. Could you explain how that would work?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was handed the decision at the end of July, and in that decision, it stated that I was an employee of the police station as of the 1st of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I could ask the registrar to assist -- the usher to assist us, please, with two documents. I'm happy to provide my copy if it is easier, but they are 00 -- P0042864 and P0042846. The dates would be 10th of July, 1992, and the 24th of June, 1992. Again, that's 004268 -- 86 -- sorry, 0042864 and 42846.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Looking at the document of 24th of June, 1992, which is also issued out of -- well, it has the same caption as the last document. I would ask you to take a look at the last paragraph, please, and if you could read us, please -- I'm sorry to impose this on you, but in the absence of any other means, if you could read slowly, so there can be a translation, the last paragraph. It says "Obrazlozenje." If you could do that, please. Read the whole thing.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In view of the shortage of staff in the Police Station of Prijedor, Basrak Lazar fully meets the requirements pursuant to the rules governing the internal organisation and systematization of work posts and the necessary documents, along with a request, was handed in to the Centre of the Security Services of Banja Luka on the 7th of May [as interpreted], 1991, and October 1991. Therefore, we propose that he take up the position of policeman in the Police Station of Prijedor as of the 1st of July, 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, whose signature is on this document, please? Who signed off?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simo Drljaca, the head of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises, but the date was the 7th of July, not the 7th of May. The 1st of July. I'm sorry. The 1st of July. The first of the seventh month.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And looking at the next document which was presented to you, dated the 10th of July, 1992, this document also bears the signature of Simo Drljaca. Would you please just tell us -- it says "Predmet." Just give us the line, if you will. Please read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Does he have it? No. It's 846. If you can put it on the ELMO and it's visible to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What does it say, please? Your name first appears next to the word "Predmet." Could you read that, please?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Basrak Lazar and others. Draft decision. We are dispatching it."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And what does it say -- your name appears as number 1 on a list below, and would you please read the language just above your name?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The Security Services Centre Banja Luka."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. And what is indicated in this document? What is the essence of the document, please? If you read at the bottom -- what is happening in this document?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an accompanying document to the decision sent to us from the Centre of Security Service -- of the Security Service in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were accepted already for service at that point in time. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] My learned colleague is making a conclusion. She says, "You have already been accepted," whereas there is no precise decision. These are all draft decisions. So she is manipulating the documents presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Somers. Please don't make your own conclusions, just put your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Shall I rephrase that? Shall I ask Mr. Basrak, what date do you consider yourself --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Ms. Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What date do you consider yourself to have been officially in service in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I received the decision about my employment.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask the registrar -- the usher, rather, to present a document labelled P0003409.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers, before we continue, let me ask you something. Will those -- are those documents being tendered for the first time or have they already been introduced?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is my belief, Your Honour, that these are first-time documents. They were essentially from documents seized from the Prijedor police station, and they are in the system, but I don't believe they have been submitted prior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I think that we should identify the documents, otherwise there will be confusion. So every time you present a document, either a document that has been marked for identification or it is a first-time document, because we have to have it identified, numbered, described, and so on and so forth so that we can follow. I don't know whether the Defence has copies of those documents. Does the Defence have the documents, Mr. Simic? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. I wanted to make an objection referring to that. The Prosecution case, in process of disclosure, has been terminated. Ms. Somers has said that she had the documents but that they were not disclosed, and they are documents linked to the work of the police station, both in Prijedor and Omarska, and the public security station directly related to this case, and that is why we are objecting. Those documents were hidden from the Defence teams and have been hidden to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If I may respond, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Susan Somers, may we have your response.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the documents that we present during examination of a witness would not have to be presented earlier. There was no demand for reciprocal discovery. There was no invocation of 66(B). These documents, in fact, are used and can be presented at the time of questioning the witness, as long as we can show that they are what they purport to be, that we can authenticate them or at least indicate that there is, essentially, an authentication. There is no violation whatsoever. These documents are not documents under 66 that we would have had to have provided, nor are they under 68. So the fact that we have documents coming in has no bearing on anything insofar as their cross-examination of witnesses is concerned. I would like to make sure that the Court is not put at a disadvantage by virtue of the fact that they are not previously labelled. Again, I'm terribly sorry that we had to do it in this very last-minute way. But what I can do, if the Court will permit, if we can just check the record, is assign a temporary tendered number, and then when I have translations, ask that they be admitted with the translation. I think it is not fair to the Chamber to have something in front of it that is incomprehensible. But the relevance of them is being set forth by what the witness is producing in the best way we can do, under the circumstances.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but you haven't answered the question. The Defence does not have these documents, and Mr. Krstan Simic does have the right to have these documents in order to be able to ask additional questions, if he so requires.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: It is correct we did not provide this morning a copy, and I'm very happy to give a stack of them to Mr. Simic. But in terms of prior turning over of the documents, I would not normally do so until the day of examination. My apologies do go out, and again I have no -- I didn't have anything really ready for the Bench and therefore I didn't prepare the pile for the Defence. If the Defence would like, I think we can immediately give one. It's not a problem. May I ask the usher if it's okay to transmit them to the Defence so they can have them. In terms of the marking of them for identification purposes, I'm not clear what the best way would be. If perhaps I could be advised by the registrar, or if I can just stack them at the end and we can indicate -- take a moment and then give the numbers that have been assigned for identification. I'm trying to do it by date and by evidence number that's been assigned now within the OTP's system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Madam Registrar, do you have a suggestion to make?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I would think it would be easier if, as the Prosecution proceeds, each new document gets a number. For example, we've already seen three documents, so the very first document would be 3/173. That's the next number for exhibits for the Prosecution. The second document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Registrar, I apologise. The first document -- we identify documents according to date. So shall we stick to that system? Now, the documents with the date X will be assigned number so and so.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As you wish, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Excuse me. What is the number, then? Can we have a number? Ms. Susan Somers identified the document by quoting a date. You are saying the first document, the second document, the third document. I am asking you, the document with the date mentioned, which number is it going to have? For example, number Z or whatever.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Okay. The document that was dated 10/27/92, is that right, Ms. --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, 27/10/92, October 27th, 1992, that could be labelled 3/173. Okay. The next date, I believe, is 10/7/92; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is correct? Then that would be labelled 3/174, okay? Then the next date is the 24th of June, 1992, and that will be numbered 3/175.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. I believe that this next document which I'm asking to have shown to the witness, which is dated -- it's got a range of dates, but the number on it is P003409, would be dated -- I'm sorry, would be 3/176?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, that's the next number.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you. And it can be identified on the top where it has two dates. It says 16/6 to 15/7/92. Is this document on the ELMO, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Would you please, Mr. Basrak, read out what the title of this document is.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The report on the work results of employees of the Police Station of Prijedor for the purpose of calculating their personal income for the period from 16 June until 5 July 1992."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Turning to the last page of this three-page document, there is a list at the bottom where it goes 1 through 6, and your name, does it not, appears first; is that right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What does it say after your name, please?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 1st of July, 1992, appointed or assigned to the Police Station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So that means -- please help me understand so that I don't come to conclusions that are incorrect. Does that mean that as of the 1st of July, 1992 you were assigned to the Prijedor Police Station?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received the decision but I remained in the reserve station in Tukovi.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your responsibilities while you were in Tukovi, now, they would have spanned how many months? How many months were you actually considering yourself attached to Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 29th of April, when the mobilisation was carried out. I was up there until the dismantling of the station itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: When did this dismantling occur, please?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date exactly, but it was in September or October, perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Were you working then as a police officer during the month of July 1992?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had this decision that I received which applied from the 1st of July, and I worked as assistant commander of the Tukovi station.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tell us, please, are you aware or familiar with part of the municipality of Prijedor called Carakovo?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with an individual who goes by the name of Strika? Strika.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: You never worked or commanded someone who used the name Strika?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you familiar with a person named Mrdza?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a person with the last name of Mrdza in my town.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Darko, also known as Dado, Mrdza, do you know him?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you ever go out -- excuse me one second. Did you ever go out on any type of field operation while as a police officer with this person Dado or Mr. Mrdza? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Ms. Somers. I think we are going around in circles. The witness said that he didn't know him personally, and the next question must then be, "What do you mean by 'not personally'?" Because if you ask a question like that, we have a contradiction. The witness said, "I don't know that man personally." The next question is: "Did you go with that man to ..." and so on. Because, as you can see, this makes no sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you for that correction. Your Honour, what I am trying to go is the personal -- if you're using the term "personal" literally, it is not the issue. It is the contact on operations that I'm getting at. And if there's been confusion, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you work at any time with a man called Mrdza, also known as Dado Mrdza? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you recollect the 18th of July, 1992, meeting up with an individual named Faik Hodzic in Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you possibly assist me in understanding why this individual indicated that you came to his home and, in your capacity as a police person, commanded units which took him and beat him and had him give certain pledges to the Serb nation while kissing a knife? Could that be a mistake? Could he have mistakenly identified you doing that?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I didn't go out into the field at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, whether you are familiar with the sections of Prijedor, Rankov -- I believe it's Rankovcani and Rizvanovici? Do those names sound familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Why would -- and perhaps this is completely wrong but maybe you can help clarify it; why would your name be associated with the term for "duke"? What is the term for "duke" in the Serbian language?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's "Vojvoda."

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Do you know why people would refer to you as referring to yourself as "Vojvoda" in your police capacity? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] My learned colleague did not establish at all that the witness had the nickname of "Vojvoda." Did anyone address the witness as "Vojvoda"? Did he have any information to that effect? It's a leading question asking, "Why do you think people called you 'Vojvoda'?"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you're right, Mr. Simic, but in any case, the witness can say, "Nobody ever called me that." Ms. Somers, would you please ask the witness if he knows that there are any persons calling him that. Please continue. And may I ask you at this point how much time do you need to finish with this witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: This should not be a terribly long examination. The points are fairly limited. I would estimate another 15 at most, 15 minutes at most. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that's three times more than direct examination, examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may comment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. We are not going to enter into a dialogue. I have asked this question precisely because Ms. Somers has already exceeded the duration of examination-in-chief. I don't know if it's three times as long; the registrar knows that. But it's true that the questions refer to the credibility of the witness, but we believe -- and we believe that they are relevant. But there are also exceptions to this principle. Ms. Somers, you will have another ten minutes to finish. Will you please look at your watch now, and you have another ten minutes to finish with this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I appreciate that. Because the length -- if I may just inform the Court, is because an awful lot of information appears to have been omitted yesterday that I believe was terribly relevant to the Court and would be essential for this Court to know in assessing whether or not this witness had some motive perhaps not to tell the whole truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you participate in any of the cleansing operations of Hambarine or of any of the villages I have just mentioned earlier, Rankovcani or Rizvanovici or Carakovo? Do you participate in any of the cleansing operations in any of those villages, please?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Going back to my earlier question. Can you think of any reason why you would have been singled out with the use of a nickname as well and identified as a police officer from Zagreb as one of the persons who was participating in these operations? Is there another person who has a similar name as you, who is also from Zagreb, in that area?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that. All I know is that I never participated. And I'm not quite clear about the nickname. Nobody ever addressed me by that nickname.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Did you submit to vetting, the vetting process, to continue your police status under the Dayton Agreement, the IPTF vetting status?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: There was no microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Could you repeat your answer if you did submit. The interpreters did not hear you.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And when was that, please?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry to interrupt you, Ms. Somers, but I believe that there was an answer the interpreters did not catch. Maybe you can have the answer repeated. You see the transcript. It says there is no microphone for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, Your Honour. I thought I reread the question about the vetting, and I thought his answer did come back as "Yes," page 19, line 3. Does that seem like it? I thought that was the response to it, unless it was a response to my asking him to do it. If there is any lack of clarity --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Tell us, please, when did you submit to vetting with the International Police Task Force, and did you tell them about your activities in July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember I made the application to continue work in the police. I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What year?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was in 1994, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: For working with IPTF. Now, they came into existence under Dayton.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the arrival of international forces, when they asked if somebody -- if people wanted to continue working in the police, I made the application under their regulations as a person who wished to continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So we understand each other, this was after the Dayton Accords, is that correct, after the war had effectively ended? And that was --

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Finished.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: At the end of 1995 is when the war ended under Dayton. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible answer.]

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, you worked with Miroslav Kvocka again in the Prijedor Police Station. When did he resume his duties, as far as you know, in the Prijedor Police Station?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the station in Tukovi was dismantled, he came to the Prijedor Station 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And that's where you were?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had left before. Before that, I had arrived from Tukovi to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: What was he doing when he was sent to Prijedor Station 1? What were his tasks?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the officer on duty in the station.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And you also had been an officer on duty, had you not? You were a senior officer on duty, right?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the beginning, we were of the same rank, and after awhile, I became an operative officer on duty.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And as an officer on duty, he had all rights, as far as you know? Did he have all rights of a regular police officer in Prijedor Station 1?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Was he given a weapon?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a weapon, a short-barrel gun. He had brought it with him.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: So he had a weapon when you first met him. At all times during the period of your acquaintance with him, he's been an officer with a weapon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: And do you know when he left his service at the Prijedor Police Station? When did he quit? When did he leave?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the date. All I know is that he left. He didn't work there any more. He wasn't employed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Are you aware of any disciplinary action that was taken against him at the Prijedor 1 Police Station during the time period when you and he were working there together?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Thank you for your time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, redirect. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, I will start by taking you back a little. Ms. Somers asked you if you had submitted to the International Police Force, IPTF, an application to continue working in the police. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: The IPTF, before making any decisions, did they vet persons who had made applications?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did the IPTF issue you with an approval that you may continue to work in the Ministry of the Interior of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did the IPTF ever ask you any additional questions regarding your involvement during 1992 and 1993?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, in the police system, did you change your job, your workplace?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Transferred from where to where?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Prijedor to Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1998. On the 1st of July, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I would like to go back now to the documents, parts of which my learned colleague showed you. I would like you to clarify them for the benefit of the Trial Chamber. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] First of all, I would like the witness to be shown document marked 3/173.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, will you please look at your monitor. Please look through the document first and then I will point -- draw your attention to specific parts of it. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Please let Mr. Basrak have the entire document in his hands and review it, and we will later put it back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, did you ask the witness to read the entire document or just a part of it? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] No, no. I just want him to look at the beginning and the end, and there is no need for him to read the entire document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, you can put it back. You have had a look at it and now we'll continue your testimony. Mr. Basrak, who sent this document?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Services Centre of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please read carefully the document.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Security Services Centre of Banja Luka, Public Security Station Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did the Public Security Station of Prijedor send this?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: To whom? Below the number, you have the name of the addressee. Please read that out.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Subject, Vukasin Janjic and others."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, what is the addressee? Please read that out.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Enclosed" --

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, please concentrate. You said the public security station is sending this. Each letter is addressed to somebody. To whom is this one addressed?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Security Services Centre of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Thank you. Which department does it go to in the Security Services Centre of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Department -- section for aliens, legal, and administrative affairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And what does it say?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Enactment on employment of persons enumerated here below."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please read it out.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We hereby deliver the personal files of newly-admitted employees for whom we have made applications for insurance with the competent agency, namely ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was your personal file hereby sent to the archives?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please don't be so nervous. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I would now like the witness to be shown the document marked 3/174.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, we'll follow the same sequence. Who sent this request?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Public Security Station of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: To whom?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the Banja Luka Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What is being delivered, enclosed in this document?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We hereby submit to you draft decisions for the persons enumerated here below."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What does "draft" mean? Is that a decision or a draft?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a draft decision. It's a proposal for admitting somebody into the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Does that mean, if I understood you correctly, Mr. Basrak, that the Public Security Station of Prijedor, on the 10th of July, 1992, submits a draft decision, according to which you should be admitted into the service?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, I would now like you to look at the document 3/175. Please look carefully at the entire document. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] I know we don't have much time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Simic, excuse me, but perhaps the document should be given to the witness so that he can see the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. entire document. One cannot see the document very well from the ELMO. Please, Mr. Usher, give the witness the document so that he can see specifically the signature. Is that okay? Thank you. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you for your assistance, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Please look at this document. It's short. Have you read it?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Does this draft decision --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, I have to interrupt you. Can we please have the document back on the ELMO now. Please. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, does Mr. Drljaca hereby propose a decision admitting you into the police service at the Public Security Station of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: To whom is this proposal addressed? And who made decisions on your employment at that time?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Security Services Centre of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you know who the chief was then?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I would like to ask you now to find in this draft decision the third line, after the words "in Zagreb 1997," and read what is written there.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Currently a member of the reserve force of the Police Station of Tukovi."

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, is that the reserve Police Station in Tukovi where you worked then and also in June and July 1992?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you work there in June?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: How long before the dismantling of the Tukovi station did you leave Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: About a month or two before that. I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, you mentioned that you were a reserve policeman in Tukovi; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You said that from the 1st of July you received the decision on your employment and that you received that decision in the end of July; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, did a reserve policeman -- a member of the reserve police force, for the duration of his employment, does he have the obligation to -- is he entitled to a salary during drills and so on?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not -- I didn't receive a salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When did you begin working as a member of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I started working on the 24th -- I'm sorry, on the 29th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: And you did not receive a single salary as a member of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember. I think there was a symbolic sum.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: I'm not asking you about the amount. We know what the salaries were like in those times. I asked you whether you had received any remuneration at all as a member of the reserve police force from April until you became an active-duty policeman.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Was that payment made to you at the same time when it was made to professional policemen? Or were there any professional policemen at the Police Station of Tukovi?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions for this witness. I'm sorry. We have a problem with the transcript so I'll ask my question again in order to correct the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Basrak, up to your arrival - you said it was the 1st of July, 1992 - until the arrival of Mr. Kvocka at the reserve Police Station of Tukovi, had there been working, according to the assignments, one active-duty policeman?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember there was. But after that, two active-duty policemen arrived. After Kvocka's arrival, two active-duty policemen arrived. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. We have clarified a small confusion in the transcript. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Krstan Simic. Judge Fouad Riad.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Basrak.

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I would just like you to shed some light on a point which you happened to repeat in your examination-in-chief. You mentioned more than once that Mr. Kvocka was considered a traitor by the community in Prijedor. You said that the media treated him, considered him as a traitor because he helped non-Serbs in the

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: (redacted). Now, in a situation of conflict -- MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: -- in the situation that existed --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Krstan Simic has a question to raise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wasn't following on my headphones. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I don't have a question. I do apologise to Judge Riad. I just wanted to observe that Judge Fouad Riad was mentioning things that we discussed in closed session. He mentioned a name there that was raised in closed session. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we need to take the appropriate steps, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So for this question, we will go into private session for a few seconds only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Judge Wald, thank you too. We have no further questions, Mr. Basrak, so you have completed your testimony here at the International Criminal Tribunal. We wish to thank you. I'm sorry. I see Mr. Fila on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, it's a rather unusual situation for us as this Defence team. A part of these documents that were given to Krstan Simic by the Prosecution as the Kvocka Defence team, we did not receive any of those documents, but in one of those documents the name of Mladjo Radic is mentioned, whom I am defending. So my question is: Can I ask a question regarding that document? Because in addition to the name Miroslav Kvocka, there is the name Mladjo Radic. So there are several questions. First of all, that document should be given to all of us, all Defence teams; secondly, I wish to remind Your Honours that these are documents which were confiscated from the Prijedor Police Station, and Omarska, I'm not sure, but in Prijedor at least. They are documents that we have never seen. There may be things in there that would be of interest to the Defence in accordance with Rule 66(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence. So my request is to ask the witness a question, to show him this document, and ask him what is in the heading, with the permission of Your Honours. I can also explain why that is important, if I'm instructed to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, let us address both questions; first, the documents for the Defence teams, and the second question is to give you a chance to put a question to the witness. Ms. Susan Somers, first question. Documents for the other Defence counsel. We have a unified concept of defence. I do not want to suggest your answer, but what is your response to this first question regarding documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honours, first of all, only five documents or six documents from this stack which we presented to counsel were used, so I, of course, would ask counsel for the rest back because they're not entitled to the balance, just what we're using. Secondly, if, in fact, there is something on the document that I didn't ask about but if -- and if you could tell me, is it -- what is the date of the document you're referring to? Is it the -- the one that has the range of 16/7 to 15/8? Yes, yes, yes. Of course. Thank you. I have it. This was not one of the documents which we asked to have examined. It was not one of the documents, and, therefore, I'm not seeking its admission. I don't think it had a --

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It has been marked as 3/ --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Wait a minute, please. Wait a minute. If you're talking at the same time, we can't follow you. Ms. Susan Somers, you need an indication regarding the document referred to by the Radic defence. Do you need that information? Then wait. Mr. Fila is going to tell you. But you must wait. Otherwise, the interpreters can simply not follow, as you know. We have been working in this courtroom for a long time, and you all know that we need to make pauses. It is simply not possible to speak at the same time. The interpreters cannot interpret two speakers at the same time, not to mention the court reporters as well. So, please, Ms. Susan Somers, wait for Mr. Fila to give you his reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I saw the document on the ELMO. Otherwise, I wouldn't know that the name of Mladjo Radic appears on it. You yourself saw it. This document has been used. My question is -- it has been marked 3/176. On page 3 of that document -- and I would like the usher to place it on the ELMO so that we know what we're talking about so I can explain my interest in it, please. Can it be placed on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: If Your Honour would allow me to comment, because I think it's a different document.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't finished yet. Page 3, which has already been shown. Could the usher turn to page 3, please. As you can see, under number 7, it says "Radic Mladjo." The Defence would like to explain the gist of our question. We would like the witness to read out the title of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. Fila. We haven't got that far yet. I made a distinction between two questions. One question was to give Ms. Susan Somers a chance to respond to your request to have this document. Ms. Susan Somers needed to know which document you were referring to as mentioning Mr. Radic. Now Ms. Susan Somers knows what document you're talking about, so we can go on to the second question, and that is whether you will have a chance to put a question to the witness. So wait now.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I just wanted to explain why I was asking for this document, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, in the heading, something is stated over which we spent at least eight hours of hearings discussing, and that is whether the Omarska Police Station in Omarska was a police station or a police station department, and now the Prosecution is showing us a document in which it says that it is a department of the police station. I personally spent at least three hours on this issue, and we now have a document proving this. That is the reason why I'm asking for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. Ms. Susan Somers, you have information regarding the document we are talking about, number 3/176, page 3, where, as number 7, the name of "Radic" is mentioned. The question now is: Are you going to give the documents to the other Defence counsel?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, of course. If there is a mention of it, there is no problem. Again, we would restrict the distribution only to those documents which we have used, and, of course, I do wish to get back the others. There is no problem. Absolutely correct position. I'm sorry. We had a document that looked similar when I expressed concern before. Yes, fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The other question -- excuse me, Mr. Simic. We have to organise ourselves a little. The other question is: What is your opinion regarding the request of Mr. Fila to put a question to the witness on this document?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: I have no objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, to see what we're going to do next, I think that Mr. Krstan Simic was on his feet. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, let Mr. Fila finish with his statement, and then I wanted to raise the issue of the return of documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The wish of Defence counsel is the following: For the witness to read out the heading of this document and the names of the persons from 1 to 12, and then I can ask him what that means. Would you please do that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, you may put the question to the witness, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: The Omarska Police Station Department. Page 3, please. Page 3, please. Have you seen it? It says: "The Omarska department of the police station." Does that mean that in Omarska there was a police station department and not a police station, and are the persons listed from 1 to 12, from 1 to 12, persons who were policemen in that department?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible answer]

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said, "Yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was rather like an examination-in-chief. Do you have a cross-examination now?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: The reference, then, of course, is to active duty police officers, would that be correct, insofar as Radic is concerned? I'm sorry, your answer, could you speak into the microphone, please? Active duty?

utterances.speaker: LAZAR BASRAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know Radic and Kvocka. I am not familiar with the others. They were probably active duty, but it's not stated here. It doesn't say so.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: No further questions. Thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Fila, you have no other questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you. I would just like this document to be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. Krstan Simic, you have another question? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honours, Ms. Somers requested us to return the documents to her because she considers them relevant for this -- not to be relevant for this case in general. We consider everything that is relevant to the Prijedor Police Station to be relevant for our case, and to illustrate that, let me refer to a document in which it says: "The Prijedor Police Station, the Tukovi station, list of members of the reserve police force for personal incomes for May 1992," and number 1 is "Mr. Basrak Lazar."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the fact that the Prosecution was willing to give the stack of documents without separating out the ones that were going into evidence is no different than when we give a stack to the Bench and we don't use them or if we tender something and the Bench says, "No, it is not admitted." They are returned to us. These are not the property of Mr. Simic. We gave a courtesy stack so that they were not disadvantaged. There is no right to these documents. The fact that they may be relevant is not the issue here. We did not put them in. They are not theirs to use at this point in time, and I think that the discussion doesn't need to go beyond that. I did not raise these points, and I would ask simply, in a professional manner, that they are returned as they are our documents. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, may I respond?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you understand correctly, you are making a distinction between the documents that you gave to Mr. Simic but that he should return to you those that you did not use. As for the others, he can keep them. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I must say I'm surprised by the position of my learned friend, that they are giving us documents as a courtesy, documents on the basis of which they are cross-examining. This is directly against the possibility of the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Krstan Simic. That courtesy was with respect to the documents that she did not use. The other documents were an obligation for her to disclose to you, the ones that she did use. Allow me to consult with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What the Chamber has decided is that the Defence is going to keep the documents which were used, and the Prosecutor is going to distribute the documents to all co-counsel, all the documents that were used and that were temporarily marked for identification. The other documents that were not used will be returned to the Prosecutor. That's clear. Yes, Mr. Fila, to finish this discussion.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Could the Chamber please consider Rule 66(B) of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, because I am surprised by these documents that the Prosecution is pulling out of its sleeve when they wish. I wish to remind the Chamber that a very, very -- that there's a very, very important document that I cannot find, and that is the schedule of shifts, you will probably recall, in the Omarska camp. At the request of the Prosecution, virtually all documents were taken away from the Prijedor Police Station and were never returned to it - allow me to explain - and those documents are in the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Mr. Fila. With all due respect, we have a witness in the courtroom now. We must have respect for the witness who is here and for the others who are waiting. We have already decided regarding the documents that have been marked. As for the others, we have decided they be returned. I think that the question that you are raising may be an important question, and if you wish, you may submit a written motion, because it is a broader issue, and the Prosecutor can respond, because we'll start here a very extensive discussion in the area of Rule 66, and we will get lost in the discussion. So I think this is an issue that can be raised in writing. Mr. Fila, you write easily. I know that. Ms. Susan Somers is going to respond. We have made our ruling. For the moment, the decision that we have taken suffices. After that, we will see.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Basrak, as you can see, we have lengthy discussions here because our objective, as you know, is to have a fair trial but also an expeditious one. I'm saying this also for the benefit of the public who are present and frequently find these things difficult to understand. So I'm making these explanations also for the benefit of the public. Of course, I am not a professor, but we do owe respect to the public as well. So, Witness, thank you very much for coming. Finally you're going to leave, and we wish you a safe journey home. I should like to ask the usher to accompany you out, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must admit that I wasn't aware that it was a good time for the break. So we're going to have a half-hour break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated. I don't see Mr. Krstan Simic. Is he there or not? He's coming. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that my lead counsel is just coming in. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Have a rest, Mr. Krstan Simic. Take a few moments to breathe, get your breath back. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm quite ready to begin. I was just sitting with the witness. The next witness is Mr. Milan Racic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Milan Racic. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. You are now going to read the solemn declaration handed to you by the usher. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sit comfortably. Approach the microphone. Thank you for coming. You are now going to be answering questions put to you by Mr. Krstan Simic, and we'll see how we're going to proceed after that. Mr. Simic, your witness. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, we just met in the witness room so I don't have to say good morning to you again. You know that I am on the Defence team of Mr. Kvocka, together with my assistant Mr. Lukic, and I shall be asking you some questions with respect to certain events. For the record, could you start off by giving us your full name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Milan Racic.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, when were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: On the 20th of October, 1957.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: In Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Is that where you reside?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Could you make pauses between question and answer, please. Are you married?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Two children.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What do you do today? What is your job?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: I'm a haulier for heavy freight, in private business.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Since when have you been doing that job?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Since 1987 or 1988, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, did you ever work in the police force?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was your job in the police force?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: I was a policeman, a militiaman.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: In what police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: In the police stations under the Banja Luka jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: So you worked in several police stations; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When and why did you leave the police force?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: I left the police force in 1987.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was the reason?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: As you know, salaries were not particularly good in the police force and I had to do other auxiliary jobs as well. At the time, this was contrary to the Rules of Service; you weren't allowed to pursue another job. My superiors suspended me as a result and they expelled me from the police force. So later on, I began a private business of my own.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did I understand you correctly? You were sacked by the police force, were you not, because you had two jobs? You had an additional employment?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Did you agree with the decision, that decision to expel you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: No, I didn't agree with the decision reached by the disciplinary commission, and today I have filed a suit against the Secretariat of the Internal Affairs of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What is the object of that lawsuit?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: To show whether I was right or not, who is right, me or them.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Are you seeking that the decision of the disciplinary commission be overruled with respect to your sacking, that it be reversed?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, it was reversed once, but the Secretariat prolonged the proceedings because they appealed the decision, and it is still ongoing today.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You mentioned the disciplinary action and all the procedure that followed it. I'm going to ask you several questions in that regard. Who and in what way files requests for disciplinary action to be taken in any given case?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: In my day, this request for disciplinary action - and I'm talking about the time I worked on the police force - was filed by the commander or the police chief of the station to which I belonged.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who decides on the request for disciplinary action?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: The Secretary of the Secretariat. That is to say, a disciplinary commission is set up, and they are in charge of the entire proceedings. The whole case comes under their jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, if I understand you correctly, that means that the commander of the police station to which you belonged was not authorised to discipline you, to bring disciplinary action against you; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, the commander of the station makes a proposal, but it is up to the Secretariat and the Secretary of the Secretariat to decide whether to sack individuals or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let me be more precise. Does the commander of the police station, was he able to punish you and say, "You will no longer be an employee of the police force"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: No. He just makes the proposal to the Secretary of the Secretariat.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Before any decision is made, is there any disciplinary action taken? Is there a disciplinary commission?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes, and there is a disciplinary commission made up of three members.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: After the investigation is conducted, is a proposal tabled and sent to the head for him to make a ruling, a decision?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: The commission makes the decision and the head of the commission confirms it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You worked in police stations all the time.

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the Banja Luka area.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Who was the main commander, if I can use that word, in the police station?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: In the police station it is the commander who heads the station.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Are there any other superior officers or subordinate ones?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: There is the deputy commander, and the two of them head the station along with the other staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Were there any other assistants for other affairs?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, depending on the number of staff employed by the station, how many workers the station had, and depending on that, there could be an assistant commander as well, the post of assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: You never worked in the police station department or precinct, did you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Let me go back to the work you did after you left the police force and became a haulier and worked with trucks. During the war years, did you use your trucks to transport any goods in the Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you remember who you did this work for?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: At one time - and I think it was on two occasions, in fact - the company was called Vilako, the owner of the company was Ranko Vila.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Where is that company located?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: The company is located on the right-hand side of the entrance to Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: But from what direction in?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Looking at it from the Banja Luka direction, from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: When you transported these goods for the Vilako company, did anything occur which was unusual? Did you encounter anybody while you were unloading?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, I arrived at the Vilako company, and it was a company which was being constructed. There was some construction material being transported. I parked my truck, the workers were there to greet me, and I noticed a man at that particular moment who was riding a bicycle, and he was wearing a uniform, and Mr. Vila, Ranko Vila, came to meet me.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me restate the question. You said you saw a man on a bicycle, wearing a uniform. What kind of uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: He was wearing a police uniform, the standard regular type of summer police uniform. He probably had a shirt underneath and a summer police jacket over it.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What happened to the cyclist? Where was he going?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: The cyclist came up to Ranko Vila, and they began a conversation. I was standing round my truck.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Can you remember what they said to each other?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, they were talking about looking for jobs for two young men who had no means of livelihood. They were out of work, and they wanted to find them jobs so that they could survive.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What type of job?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, working with electrical installations, something of that kind. And I know that they mentioned some names, and they were the names of two Muslim men.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Do you happen to remember those names today?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: No. It wasn't important for me, and I'm very bad at remembering names anyway. So I don't remember the names, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What was Mr. Vila's reaction?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Mr. Ranko Vila -- as I say, they were difficult times, and nobody had enough money to live on, and the man in the uniform asked that these two people be given employment, and he said that that was a problem because it was a problem to give anybody a job as there were so many people looking for jobs and that it was especially difficult to employ Muslim men, and he didn't want to have any problems in that regard, but I don't know actually what he answered, what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: What were the reactions of the person in the uniform?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, the person in the uniform wanted to make a compromise with Ranko. He was ready, as far as I was able to hear standing where I was, he himself was ready to use his free time to help those individuals, to be on the spot, and that he could be there while the two others were actually working; that he was ready to give up all his spare time to be a sort of auxiliary worker and to protect Mr. Vila from having any unpleasantness for allowing these two others, the two Muslims, to do the work, as a cover, sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, talking to me when we had our meeting, you said that the policeman who had that conversation brought himself into a very demeaning position, into a difficult position himself; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, you spent this whole unfortunate war on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Several times in your testimony so far today you used the word "unpleasantness" and that that was Mr. Vila's excuse. What, for you, does this unpleasantness mean for Mr. Vila? What would it mean? Why would he have this unpleasantness?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: Well, there were tensions at the time. Everybody was nervous. Nobody had a lot of money. There was no electricity; there was not much of anything, in fact. So even people who had jobs would have had to contend with a certain amount of unpleasantness, especially if they would take in Muslim workers rather than people of their own ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. K
utterances.text: Mr. Racic, let me be more direct. I too spent the entire war in the same area. Was there any realistic danger of isolation from the environment and situations of excess with grievous consequences for Serbs who would, in the relations that were created, who would decide to employ Muslims? Would they have -- would there be dire consequences for them?

utterances.speaker: MILAN RACIC
utterances.text: It depended, of course -- it depended on the different environment, of course, and what the time was, what period.
