utterances.text: Who handed over these prisoners from Keraterm to you and your colleagues in the van?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Well, the workers who worked there. I believe they were reserve policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And did they provide you with any kind of document or paperwork regarding these prisoners who were placed in the van at Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: The documentation had been prepared already.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: During the drive from Keraterm to Omarska, could you hear the prisoners in the back of the van moaning or asking for water?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You said that -- during your direct testimony, you said that the persons that you transported in the van to Omarska had been sentenced on the basis of state public security problems. Can you tell me what crime or crimes were these persons convicted of?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you anything about this. I was an ordinary policeman who just fulfilled the orders of his superiors. And why they had been sentenced -- I don't know what they had been convicted of.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Well, you also said during your direct testimony that part of your job as a police officer was to ensure law and order. So I'm wondering if you could explain who it was who convicted and sentenced these people that were in the van you were driving.

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that. They probably had to be taken into custody regarding issues of military or state security; they had to be taken in for questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. So now you're saying that they had not been convicted of a crime but they needed to be taken in for questioning regarding possible crimes; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell me what law provided for persons to be incarcerated or detained in camps instead of prisons? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness is not an expert to interpret laws. He can only testify to facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm not asking for an expert opinion. This question directly stems from the witness's direct examination. He said that it was part of his job to ensure law and order. If that was part of his job, he would have to have knowledge of laws. So I would like to know under what law --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Only on the level of facts, please, if he was aware of a law or regulation that he was supposed to uphold.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolta, if you knew at the time, what law provided for persons to be detained or incarcerated in camps instead of prisons?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you that. I was just an ordinary policeman. There were institutions on higher levels which made decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. Those institutions in higher levels, they issued orders, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You and your colleagues in the police department, you carried out those orders at the time, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Now, during the spring and summer of 1992, you made a total of two trips to the Omarska camp; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This first trip was between the 8th and 12th of June.

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: That was the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Oh, okay. When did you make the first trip?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I think in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I see. So in mid-May, you transported persons to the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes. Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Court's indulgence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The purpose of these trips to the Omarska camp was simply to transport these persons to the camp.

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Approximately how much time did you spend at the Omarska camp on each visit?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: It took five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. So altogether you spent a total of about ten minutes at the Omarska camp during 1992; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you were never actually assigned to work at the Omarska camp while it was in operation during 1992, were you?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No, I wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So do you have any specialised knowledge about the operation or organisation of the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No. I had no information; I didn't know what was happening there.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On that second trip that you made, bringing Mr. Nusret Sivac to the Omarska camp, eventually you were told by Mr. Kvocka, "We need his sister, (redacted)." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes. He said an error had been made with regard to Nusret and who (redacted).

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: (redacted)?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could, I would like to show a document to this witness. This was a document that was used by the Defence, I believe it was yesterday. It's been marked as D17/1. I know that the Defence has a copy; I don't know if the Trial Chamber has copies in front of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We don't have it. But in any case, if you put the document on the ELMO, we will be able to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We just have to know, is it really the document under this number, that is, D17/1?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, to be precise, this is one of the documents that now has two numbers, because it was one of the documents that was admitted into evidence a year and a half ago by Trial Chamber III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is why I'm asking the question, because, as you know, yesterday we admitted only 37, 38, and 39, I believe, but not 17. Can the registrar please identify this document? Right. We're going to look into it. Please continue, Mr. Saxon. Do we have the document on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolta, would you take a look at the document that's by your side on the ELMO, please. If you could, take a look at the date on that document. Do you see the date?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you read that date, please? Can you read that date out loud, please?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: "For expedient and the soon restoration of peace in the territory of Prijedor --"

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. Bolta. If you could simply read the date that is on the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: 1st May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, I believe the witness is inadvertently misreading the date on that document. The document I'm looking at says 31 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question, Mr. Saxon, is whether the document you're looking at is the same as the document the witness has. Can you please check it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, it is the same document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, then, perhaps we should put the document on the ELMO so that everyone can see it here. I believe we can see it. The question, Witness, was: What date do you see in the top left-hand corner of the page?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: The 1st of May, 1992. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and we see the same thing. I believe that perhaps there is a problem here, Mr. Saxon. I believe that everyone, even the public, if the document should be made public, will see -- will read here the 1st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, Mr. Saxon, you have the floor. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise for the quality of the copy that has been placed on the ELMO. The final English translation of this document says "31 May 1992." We have a problem with the quality of the copy of the B/C/S version. At this point, I don't want to prolong this any more; I will remove the document at this time and move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We really have to know what the date is because if everybody -- as everybody can see, there is a genuine reason for this confusion. So if you withdraw your question, then it doesn't matter. You can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Just as a point of clarification, Your Honour. On the exhibit log prepared by the Registry, this document has the date 31 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: And, Mr. Saxon, I can see the trace of "3." There is the trace of "3."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RIAD
utterances.text: You have to look very clearly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mentioned the name. I said that you were mentioned -- confirmed that the Registry has the date on this document as the 31st of May. Can you comment on that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I do have on my log the 31st of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we know how you managed to obtain that date?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm just referring to my log. I don't have the document in front of me because the usher has it on the ELMO, but I imagine that my predecessor got the date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolta, if the date of this document is 31 May 1992 - and I apologise for the poor quality of the copy - is it possible then that you are mistaken when you say you first transported prisoners to the Omarska camp in mid-May 1992?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If you take a look at this document and read paragraph 1, paragraph 1 says that: "The industrial compound of the Omarska mine shall serve as a provisional collection centre for persons captured in combat or detained on the grounds of the Security Service's operational information." So is it possible -- and then this document is signed by Simo Drljaca. Is it possible that you are slightly mistaken regarding the date of your first trip to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot remember exactly when the first time was, but I believe it was in May.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you very much. I will move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: If that document could be removed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolta, on that first occasion when you transported people to Omarska, do you recall who you transported?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I don't know the persons. I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Do you know their --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, wait a moment, please. Yes, Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just wishing to help Mr. Saxon and the others. If you look at charge 6 of the indictment, also prepared by the Prosecution, by the Prosecutor's Office, it says: "Between the 24th of May and the 30th of August, the Bosnian Serb authorities took away to Omarska ..." So you, Mr. Saxon, claim that they were taken away to camps on the 24th of May, that is, before the 30th. We can see a trace of another number there, but what number, we don't know. But if you could please only look at the indictment. That's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you recall the ethnicity of the persons who you transported on the first occasion to the Omarska camp? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection. Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] The witness said he didn't know the people whom he had taken away to Omarska, and how could he possibly then know their ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: May I respond, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not necessary for me because we have to know what "not to know" means. He maybe doesn't know the people, Mr. Simic, their names, their parents, their age, but they may be familiar to him. We will only know when the witness answers. So, Mr. Saxon, please ask the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Bolta, did you know the ethnicity of the persons --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Saxon, excuse me. To make things quite clear, Witness, when you say you did not know the persons in the van, what did you really mean? You didn't know them. What did you mean when you said that?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I didn't know the people. How can I know about them when I didn't know them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In any event, put your question to the witness, Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I will move on, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what crime or crimes were these persons accused of?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I don't know for what crimes. It was not in my competency.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did you know if these persons were dangerous people?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I didn't know those people. I didn't know what persons were involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Were these persons handcuffed when they were in the van?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe their physical condition?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Well, they were normal people. They varied in build. I don't know what you mean by "physical condition."

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe if any of them showed signs of beating or other kinds of mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I couldn't notice because I sat inside the vehicle and I didn't watch them as they were entering.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: How were these people dressed? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I think they were in their civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When persons were detained in the Prijedor area and sent to a detention facility, were they normally left in their civilian clothes or were they given some other kinds of clothing to wear? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness said he spent only five minutes each time there before going back. So I really don't know where this questioning is going, because the witness has already answered this, and what could he have possibly seen in five minutes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, but let the witness answer. Mr. Saxon, please proceed. I'm sorry. Continue, but I must tell you that your time has almost expired. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you transported these persons, did you transport them from the police station in Prijedor to the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Well, the first part of the trip was from the police station and then it was in two stages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe the stages of this trip?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Well, the first trip was from the Public Security Station of Prijedor, and then from Keraterm, where the people who had already been prepared entered the vehicle, and we went to Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: So again or, rather, on that first trip as well, your van stopped in Keraterm, picked up prisoners, and took them to Omarska?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can you describe the condition of the prisoners who you picked up in Keraterm?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: I cannot because I didn't see enough of those people to describe their condition. I believe they entered the van normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did the people who entered the van at Keraterm make any sounds that you could hear?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did they ask you for anything?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: When you arrived at the Omarska camp on that first visit, who did you turn these prisoners over to?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: At the entrance, the same way as the second time I went there, there was a reserve policeman on duty there. He took over those people, Tomo Stojakovic gave him the list, and we turned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: On that first occasion, how were the prisoners treated when they were removed from the police van?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: Again, they were searched, also in a rough manner, not quite in accordance with the Rules of Service in the Security Service, as I have already testified for the other occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Did anyone intervene to prevent this mistreatment at that time?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: The first time, no one did. As soon as the persons got off, I turned the vehicle around and went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: You yourself did not intervene when you saw these prisoners being treated roughly, did you?

utterances.speaker: BRANE BOLTA
utterances.text: No. I was sitting in the vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: The Court's indulgence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you. At this stage, I would like to know whether we can finish with this witness or not. So I would like to know how much more time you need for your re-examination, Mr. Krstan Simic. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I will need 10 to 15 minutes. I would prefer us to address the question of protective measures, if we may, as we have prepared a submission and we need your assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me ask Mr. Stojanovic also, how much time, roughly, you need for your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we will have about three questions and I think they will take less than five minutes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So we'll resume tomorrow. In any event, regarding your request, Mr. Krstan Simic, briefly, please. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] But we need to have the witness seen out, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, you're quite right. So, Witness, you will continue your testimony tomorrow. We have not been able to complete it today so we'll see you again tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Simic, thank you for drawing my attention to this. You have the floor now. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have prepared my submission and I appeal to the registrar to accept it. Could I hand it over to the registrar, please. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Ms. Susan Somers.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOMERS
utterances.text: Pardon me for interrupting both counsel and the Bench, but is this any new submission or is this a submission we already have?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think I myself am trying to find my way in this connection. What is your aim, Mr. Krstan Simic? Because we don't have stamps here to stamp requests with. MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is an identical submission to the previous one, only the list of names has been reduced as some witnesses have already testified. Certain facts have been added, and the pseudonyms are given, in agreement with the Registry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But, Mr. Krstan Simic, you will give that to the Registry and then it will reach us through the Prosecution and the Registry will do its job. After all, this is not the Registry's Office. We are in hearing here in the courtroom. So give your submission to the Registrar and then they will process it. Is that all you wanted to say, Mr. Krstan Simic? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes. I will be guided by your decision. But I do appeal to Your Honours, to the Bench, to make a decision as soon as possible because we will have a problem with witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If we have your submission today, you will have a decision tomorrow. There's no problem. Does that suit you? MR. K. SIMIC: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but there is a certain protocol that we have to observe. Tomorrow we will resume at 9.20. See you all tomorrow at 9.20.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
